# Independent bounded review: source siblings and the smooth PF control

Date: 2026-09-17.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review.
Verdict: ACCEPT_LIMITED_SOURCE_SIBLINGS_AND_PF_CONTROL.
Disposition: no mathematical correction required in S1--S3 or M1--M4.
Status: exploratory isolated PAPER review, not a canonical supplier.
Original full V positivity and RH remain open.

## 1. Frozen candidate, pins, and review scope

Candidate: `SOURCE_SIBLINGS_AUDIT.md`.
SHA256: `d30a25ed1ad904ecb0e45d14af81981cf399853c190ce1d5a8b2ce0a5d505852`.
Bytes: 15764. LF: 307.
Pin manifest: `SOURCE_PINS.json`.
SHA256: `0a868ee4ff1b7d9e4c4a2c3a41625383c6be5b3260a7853c2cc1e3b4b94d341b`.

I read the complete candidate, the specified primary HTML bodies at the
locators below, and the relevant named project sections. All manifest
hashes were recomputed and matched. The parent check was not used as an
input to the mathematical verdict. This review writes only its assigned
staging file and performs no repository, control, queue, publication,
external-send, descendant-agent, or search action.

The review verifies two exact source identifications and a bounded
negative control for an invalid general implication. It does not import
the general extra-factor Sheffer Theorem 1. It does not promote positive
matrix densities to the original V sign or to a theorem about xi zeros.
The received MELLINEDGE theorem is used as its pinned accepted input;
its earlier prime-phase proof is not independently repeated here.

## 2. Exact primary and project bindings

Primary A: Cheon--Forgacs--Tran, arXiv 2508.18229v1,
`2508.18229v1.html`:
`5a633292a613289ca6b54d2b1f584d75cdf2b463861387f96bc733a62931f9c1`.
Read the complete Section 2, especially equations (2.7), (2.12),
(2.18)--(2.23), and Theorems 5, 9, 11. The introductory quotation in the
candidate matches this primary HTML. The review concerns this exact v1;
it makes no assertion about an unread journal version.

Primary B: Forster--Kieburg--Kosters, arXiv 1710.08794v4,
`1710.08794v4.html`:
`8f7e6b2119ee58ec31515c31dc8aa50769abdc0ce5654c437d756e76a642603b`.
Read Section 2.1's distinction between G and M_0, Definitions 2.2--2.3
and 2.7, Theorems 2.9--2.10, equation (2.27), and the proofs in Section
4.2, including the derivative and boundary hypotheses. The candidate's
short quotation of Theorem 2.9(1) matches the primary statement.

Pinned project inputs, relative to the isolated worktree:

- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-12_THETA_TN_INFINITY_INTAKE.md`:
  `ae39ab4cbbfae7ad8c04b61dfb9828c6e9efa0247a538da72e4bd3e748de3790`.
  Lines 33--66 supply actual additive PF infinity, including the full limit;
  lines 68--104 distinguish it from the failed physical transfer.
- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-12_FULL_SIGN_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md`:
  `1e296a504631b58beb7863f4c7f36174bd08876cfc7093febfe00cc8306a5282`.
  Lines 15--23 and 47--81 fix r, Phi, normalization, reciprocity, endpoint
  envelopes and the exact Mellin factor 2xi(s).
- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-15_RH_ROUTE_AUDIT.md`:
  `0978708a88fb2c4802ed3405b37b427ab6890b46a8ffa688edfe757c4a4fe4e3`.
  Lines 127--164 distinguish additive Laplace and Mellin transforms;

- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-16_MELLINEDGE_INTAKE.md`:

Receipt hashes also match the manifest:

They bind provenance; they are not mathematical proof inputs or evidence

## 3. S1--S3: exact Laguerre/Sheffer specialization and source recovery

PASS; candidate lines 57--126.

At p=-1/2, p*=0, alpha_0=1 and N=0, primary A's (2.7) is exactly

    sum q_j(u) w^j/j! = (1-w)^(u-1/2)(1+w)^(-u).

The Appell coefficients in (2.18) reduce to the identity because the
falling factorial (0)_k vanishes for positive k. The resulting Laguerre
parameter is -p-1=-1/2, so phi_j(v)=j!L_j^(-1/2)(v)exp(-v/2) is exact.
In particular, there is no missing v^(-1/4) prefactor from the distinct
Laguerre-function convention discussed earlier in the primary paper.

The ordinary Laguerre generating formula gives

    sum phi_j(2v) w^j/j!
      =(1-w)^(-1/2) exp[-v(1+w)/(1-w)].

For Re(u)>0 and w in a sufficiently small complex disk, the real part
of (1+w)/(1-w) is positive uniformly on a smaller disk. This supplies
an integrable bound at infinity; v^(Re(u)-1) supplies one at zero.
Integration and coefficient extraction are therefore justified and give
Gamma(u)q_j(u). Rescaling v=pi k^2 t and summing for Re(s)>1 gives the
factor pi^(-s/2) sum k^(-s)=pi^(-s/2)zeta(s), with no factor of two.
For each fixed j, the absolute Laguerre polynomial integral is finite,
so the same k-series proves absolute interchange. No assertion about
separate improper integrals outside this half-plane is needed.

Direct calculation gives

    q_2(u)=4u^2-2u+3/4,
    2!L_2^(-1/2)(v)=v^2-3v+3/4.

Substitution v=2pi k^2 t proves term by term, in convergent full series,

    psi_2(t)-(3/4)psi_0(t)=t r(t).

Hence q_2(s/2)-3/4=s(s-1), and the Mellin integral of the combined
source is exactly 2xi(s). The combined integral converges for every s
because the actual r decays exponentially at infinity and faster than
any power at zero. Thus its entire continuation is legitimate. The
cancellation in the combined integrand is not permission to treat the
individual psi integrals as entire improper integrals.

The recurrence follows directly from differentiating the generating
function:

    q_(j+1)=(1/2-2u)q_j+j(j-1/2)q_(j-1).

After p_j(v)=i^j q_j(1/4+iv) and P_j=2^(-j)p_j, the recurrence becomes

    P_(j+1)=v P_j-[j(j-1/2)/4]P_(j-1),
    P_0=1, P_1=v.

Its Jacobi matrix has adjacent entries sqrt(k(k-1/2))/2. These entries
are real and strictly positive for k>=1. The matrix is real symmetric,
and an eigenvector with zero first coordinate would vanish successively
in all coordinates. Every eigenspace is therefore at most one dimensional;
symmetry gives diagonalizability, proving simple real eigenvalues. This
proves the critical-line zero statement for the specialized q_j(s/2)
without importing general Theorem 1 or its extra factors.

A hypothetical off-line nontrivial zeta zero is still a zero of the
continued product q_j(s/2)pi^(-s/2)Gamma(s/2)zeta(s): all other factors
are finite there and the gamma factor is nonzero. The elementary logical
control and the report's factor-versus-product distinction are correct.
S3 recovers xi itself, not a sequence whose zero location has been proved
for the complete transform.

## 4. M1: smooth full source and normalized ensembles for every n

PASS; candidate lines 128--150.

The full series gives, for each fixed derivative order at infinity,
polynomial factors times an exponential exp(-pi t) bound (or a weaker
fixed exponential bound sufficing equally). Differentiated reciprocity
expresses each derivative near zero as a finite sum of powers of t times
r^(k)(1/t). Exponential decay at 1/t beats all of those powers. Every
right derivative consequently tends to zero at zero. The zero extension
is C infinity and Schwartz, with all absolute polynomial derivative
moments. It is nonnegative, nonzero, supported in [0,infinity), and has
mass one by the accepted source law.

Together with the pinned full additive PF-infinity theorem, these facts
verify Definition 2.3(1) for every fixed n. Theorem 2.9(1) applies in each
dimension using the SAME source; no relation between dimension and a
finite theta or gamma cutoff is introduced.

With Delta_n(a)=det[a_k^(j-1)] and the candidate's derivative orientation,
the moment matrix is

    M_ij=int a^(i-1)(-d/da)^(j-1)r(a) da.

All integration-by-parts boundary terms vanish. M_ij=0 for i<j and
M_jj=(j-1)! since int r=1. Andreief's identity therefore gives the full
R^n integral n! times product_(j=0)^(n-1)j!. The candidate C_n is correct
for the symmetric density on all eigenvalue configurations, as in the
primary definition. The primary theorem supplies nonnegativity.

This positive probability density is not [V(x_i,x_j)], and the candidate
makes no equality with V, variance identity, cross-dimensional coupling,
or xi spectral assertion.

## 5. M2: nu=0 gamma lift, Mellin zeros, and failed reciprocity

PASS; candidate lines 152--187.

Theorem 2.10 requires a nonzero nonnegative PF function of order n in the
Hermitian derivative class with support in [0,infinity). These conditions
were all verified for r. At nu=0, the factor 1/Gamma(nu+1) is one and the
power (x/t)^nu is one; equation (2.27) is exactly M2. The theorem itself
supplies the output derivative and boundary conditions of Definition
2.3(3). It concerns the additive M_0 setting, not multiplicative G.
Primary Section 2.1 explicitly separates these two operations even
though their matrix sets agree off a null set.

Conditional on T=t, TE with E exponential of rate one has density
exp(-x/t)/t. Hence Omega is a normalized scalar probability density.
For sigma=Re(s)>0, absolute Fubini has value
Gamma(sigma)E[T^(sigma-1)]<infinity. It gives

    M_Omega(s)=Gamma(s)M_r(s)=2Gamma(s)xi(2s-2).

All real moments of T exist from the full source endpoint bounds. Gamma
is finite and zero-free on Re(s)>0, so zeros and their multiplicities are
preserved exactly there. No equality of improper Mellin integrals on a
larger half-plane is claimed.

At zero, dominated convergence by r(t)/t gives the positive finite limit
C=E[T^(-1)]. For any L>0, exp(-x/t)<=[sup z^L exp(-z)](t/x)^L gives
Omega(x)<=C_L x^(-L)E[T^(L-1)]. If Omega(1/x)=x^kappa Omega(x) held for
any fixed real kappa, choosing L>max(kappa,0) would force a positive
limit C on the left and zero on the right as x tends to infinity.
The claimed failure of every reciprocity of that power form is proved.

For the separate multiplicative theorem, omega(t)=t^(1/4)r(t) is smooth
and has the required weighted derivative moments in every finite order.
Its logarithmic input is exactly

    omega(exp(-u))exp(-u)=exp(-5u/4)r(exp(-u))=Phi(-u/2).

Theorem 2.9(2) requires the appropriate PF order of this input for each n;
requiring all n is PF infinity. Reflection and positive dilation preserve
that property, so the pinned failure for Phi excludes the proposed
all-size multiplicative premise. This does not assert failure of every
individual finite order.

## 6. M3--M4: one smooth PF source retains an off-edge Mellin zero

PASS; candidate lines 189--243.

The pinned accepted theorem applies to the literal T_N with rates pi k^2
and shape two. Choose one fixed sufficiently large N and one zero s_0
in 11/8<Re(s)<2. The transform is holomorphic on this strip, is positive
at real s>1, and is not identically zero. Its zeros are isolated, allowing
a disk D around s_0 lying in the strip with zero-free boundary. No simple
zero or effective numerical root is required.

Each r_N is a finite convolution of one-sided exponential densities;
therefore it is PF infinity even though it lacks unrestricted smoothness
at zero. Scaling full r by epsilon>0 preserves PF infinity, and additive
convolution preserves it by the accepted continuous Cauchy--Binet argument.
Thus r_(N,epsilon) is PF infinity for every positive epsilon.

The full scaled r is Schwartz with flat zero extension. Differentiation
of its convolution with r_N is valid to every order. More explicitly,
weighted L1 bounds follow from

    int (1+|x|)^k |(r_N*g)^(j)(x)|dx
      <= [int (1+|y|)^k r_N(y)dy]
         [int (1+|v|)^k |g^(j)(v)|dv],

where g(t)=epsilon^(-1)r(t/epsilon). The analogous weighted sup bound
follows using the sup norm of the second factor. Finite moments of r_N
therefore give smoothness, all polynomial derivative moments, and even
the Schwartz bounds. Both factors have nonnegative support, so the
smooth zero extension is flat at zero.

For each fixed epsilon>0, T_(N,epsilon)>=epsilon T' gives every negative
moment; positive moments follow from the sum of variables with all
positive moments. In particular, ONE fixed smoothed source meets M1 and
M2 in every matrix dimension. No choice of epsilon depending on dimension
is needed, and the finite regularity of r_N has not been mistaken for
infinite regularity.

For any compact K in Re(s)>1 and almost every realization T_N>0, the
function (T_N+epsilon T')^(s-1) is jointly continuous on K times a small
closed epsilon interval. It converges uniformly in s on K as epsilon
approaches zero. For epsilon<=1 the difference supremum is bounded by
2[1+(T_N+T')^B], B=max(1,sup_K Re(s)-1), which is integrable. Dominated
convergence of that supremum gives the claimed locally uniform Mellin
convergence, not just pointwise convergence in s. Holomorphy on a
neighborhood of D follows from the same power moments; logarithmic
factors are absorbed by a margin to Re(s)=1 and a higher positive moment.

The positive minimum of |M_N| on the boundary of D now pays Rouche's
inequality for every sufficiently small epsilon. The smoothed transform
has the same positive number of zeros inside D, counting multiplicity.
Gamma has no zero or pole on D, so the gamma lift retains these zeros.
They lie strictly to the right of Re(s)=5/4.

Finally, E[T]-E[T_N]>0, being the omitted positive gamma tail. Taking
epsilon smaller also than (E[T]-E[T_N])/E[T] makes the new mean strictly
less than the full source mean. This additional bound is compatible with
the Rouche-smallness condition and proves that the control is a different
source. There is no claimed explicit N, zero coordinate or epsilon bound.

The resulting counterexample refutes the generic implication from smooth
additive PF infinity and all-size positive ensembles ALONE to the stated
Mellin zero-free half-plane. No weighted reciprocity for this control was
proved or used. It therefore does not refute a mechanism that really uses
PF together with the original reciprocity, and it produces no negative
row of the original theta V.

## 7. Final scope and acceptance

ACCEPT_LIMITED_SOURCE_SIBLINGS_AND_PF_CONTROL, bound to the exact candidate
and source hashes above.

The Sheffer specialization recovers the full arithmetic transform but
leaves its zeta factor uncontrolled. The Hermitian and nu=0 additive lifts
are valid positive constructions in every dimension, with the stated
normalization and hypotheses. Their positivity has no established bridge
to the original V. The gamma lift preserves rather than repairs Mellin
zeros, loses weighted reciprocity, and the smooth PF control rigorously
blocks a PF/ensemble-positivity-only inference.

These are limited exact identifications and rejection filters. They are
not a new positive source mechanism, an improved V bound, a spectral
construction proving RH, or canonical admission. The candidate consistently
retains that boundary and correctly records incomplete search coverage.

# Parent check of source sibling candidate

Candidate d30a25ed1ad904ecb0e45d14af81981cf399853c190ce1d5a8b2ce0a5d505852.
The following are direct algebraic/analytic checks, not a numerical RH test.

1. Read actual arXiv HTML theorem bodies and formulas, not Consensus abstracts.
At p*=0 the falling factorial (0)_(n-k) vanishes unless n=k. Thus the
paper's umbral composition reduces precisely to n! L_n^(-1/2), with no
unaccounted constant. Mellin integration of its generating function gives
Gamma(u)(1-w)^(u-1/2)(1+w)^(-u). The fixed-j theta sum is absolutely
integrable for Re(s)>1. q2(s/2)-3/4=s(s-1), and tr has the same coefficients
4pi^2 k^4 t^2-6pi k^2t. Full normalization agrees with the reread transfer
audit. No separate divergent integral is analytically continued as an
improper integral.

2. Differentiation yields (1-w^2)Q_w=(1/2-2u+w/2)Q. Comparing exponential
coefficients gives q_(j+1)=(1/2-2u)q_j+j(j-1/2)q_(j-1). Multiplication by
i^(j+1) at u=1/4+iv gives +2v and minus j(j-1/2). Dividing by 2^(j+1)
gives the stated monic Jacobi recurrence with beta_j=j(j-1/2)/4>0.
Characteristic-polynomial recurrence and eigenvector recursion prove real
simple roots without a new external zero theorem. A finite entire
polynomial cannot cancel a zero of zeta in its holomorphic critical strip.

3. Both input spaces in source B were read. Additive r satisfies its
finite-n derivative/moment hypotheses by endpoint exponential bounds and
reciprocity. Confluence of positive translation minors also directly gives
the nonnegative derivative determinant in M1 for ordered a_k: expand
r(a_k-epsilon(j-1)) in the row variable, divide by the positive Vandermonde
in epsilon(j-1), and let epsilon downarrow0. The resulting row derivatives
are (-partial)^(j-1)r/(j-1)!. Thus the sign agrees with Delta_n. Repeated
integration by parts and Andreief give n! product j!, with no hidden
nonpositive normalization. No covariance or spectral identity with V is
available from this calculation.

4. For the nu=0 mixture, integral exp(-x/t)x^(s-1)dx/t equals
Gamma(s)t^(s-1). Absolute Fubini is licensed for every Re(s)>0. Omega has
positive finite limit E(1/T) at zero, and faster than any inverse-power
decay at infinity. The proposed reciprocal identity would contradict
these two endpoint limits for every fixed real exponent. The direct GL
criterion concerns omega(exp(-u))exp(-u), which at critical omega is exactly
Phi(-u/2), not r. Therefore only the additive positive-ensemble application
has satisfied hypotheses.

5. The finite-source MELLINEDGE input was reread at its exact pinned
intake: its s0 exists for any chosen sufficiently large fixed N, in the
open strip (11/8,2), at arbitrarily high positive imaginary heights. For
M4 only one such zero and one disk are used. PF is preserved under the
ordinary convolution, while the scaled full source makes the extension
smooth with all derivative moments. Negative moments follow from the
lower bound by epsilon T'. Uniform dominated convergence on compacts of
Re(s)>1 uses positive real powers, not any possibly divergent inverse
moment of raw T_N. A small compact enlargement absorbs logs for
holomorphy. Rouche preserves multiplicity count in the chosen disk; no
simple zero or explicit epsilon is required. This is one smooth PF source
with positive ensembles of every n but an off-edge Mellin zero. It is
not reciprocal by assumption and supplies no original-theta V witness.

6. Search chronology honestly records the new shelf dictionaries running
after external discovery; INCOMPLETE freshness receipts remain incomplete.
No novelty, exhaustive coverage, full V sign, RH proof/refutation, Lean
validation, canonical admission or sign-counter reset is certified.
accepted: Full theta density tr is psi2-3psi0/4 in an explicitly normalized Sheffer/Laguerre theta family
Jacobi polynomial real zeros do not control the unchanged zeta factor
Actual additive PF infinity supplies positive Hermitian ensembles in every dimension
Specified gamma mixture supplies positive M0 ensembles, preserves Mellin zeros in Re(s)>0 and loses every power reciprocal identity
Smoothing one raw finite MELLINEDGE source by convolution with epsilon full source supplies a smooth PF infinity control with all-dimension positive ensembles and an off-edge Mellin zero

No claim on joint PF plus weighted reciprocity sufficiency
No actual theta negative V witness
